debate_title: Should governments break up vertically integrated AI comp...

conflicts.point: Whether co-designed vertical integration between chips, cloud infrastructure, and foundation models is physically required for frontier scaling or merely serves as a mechanism for corporate resource capture.

positions.stance: Co-designed vertical integration and hardware-software co-location yield measurable performance and thermodynamic efficiencies that modular unbundling would destroy.
Modular engineering and open interface standards are fully compatible with frontier scaling, meaning vertical integration is an economic strategy rather than a physical necessity.

conflicts.point: Whether mandatory structural unbundling reduces or multiplies regional energy waste and grid strain.

positions.stance: Fragmenting compute load across independent regional renters multiplies total kilowatt draw by forcing duplicate power loops, backup generators, and transformer yards.
Spreading out compute loads across open facilities shares cooling and transmission infrastructure without surrendering public energy grids to private monopoly control.
